messages:
maria: heads-up — sales just escalated a request from Acme Corp for a low-latency caching toggle. they want it in the next release cycle. asking if we can bend on SLOs to ship earlier.
kevin: can you paste the ask? is it toggling a cache param or a whole new infra piece?
maria: it's a toggle + a lightweight cache shard per-tenant. engineering says ~2w of work for api + rollout controls.
sam: 2w dev + probable 1w staging validation + runbook. also introduces a cache refill storm risk on deploy.
anya: what are the current SLOs we'd be risking? p99 latency 200ms, p95 55ms. any cache could help p95 but may bump tail at p99 during cold-starts.
maria: sales quoted impact: reduces latency for Acme by ~30% and likely reduces their token cost (smaller requests). big logo.
kevin: ok. let's run a quick RICE-style back-of-envelope. Reach: Acme immediate, but could be 5% of revenue next quarter. Impact: big for that account -> 8/10. Confidence: 60% (new infra). Effort: 3 dev-weeks total.
sam: Ops perspective: toil impact if we ship without automation = +4hrs/week oncall. If we build automation, upfront cost increases but steady state lower toil.
anya: proposal: conditionally prioritize if we can meet launch criteria: 1) canary in us-west for 1 week, 2) automated cache eviction + circuit breaker, 3) documented rollback playbook.
maria: that seems fair. sales pushed timeline to next release which is 3w out. can we scope an MVP that meets those criteria?
kevin: MVP approach: limit to 10 tenants (Acme + 9), feature-flag default off, metrics + tracing added, no cross-tenant sharing. dev scope ~1.5w, canary 1w, docs 0.5w -> fits 3w.
sam: still need automation for refill backoff (prevent stampede). I can spike a token-bucket refiller pattern. 2 days.
anya: SLO gating: if p99 latency degrades by >10% or error rate increases by >0.5% during canary, automatic rollback. add alert: slo-degradation > threshold -> page oncall.
maria: can we add an explicit sales-commit: Acme will do canary in their integration test window and not enable globally until we sign off.
kevin: yes, we'll require customer coordination. also add a cost/benefit note to the PR: revenue estimate vs operational risk.
ops-bot: deploy-checklist created: checklist/2126789012-cache-toggle -> includes metrics, canary, rollback steps.
sam: +1 on checklist. schedule spike tomorrow, i'll draft refill pattern and test harness.
maria: thanks team — i'll tell sales we can tentatively commit to the 3w timeline with the gating conditions.
kevin: final decision: green if engineering delivers MVP + canary automation + runbook. otherwise hold. :thumbsup:
anya: logging action items: kevin -> implement flag + metrics; sam -> refill automation spike; maria -> customer coordination; i'll write SLO rollback playbook.
maria: perfect. closing the loop here. any objections?
nobody: (silent) :+1:
kevin: adding to roadmap board under "conditional priorities" and RICE note.
anya: also adding an entry to toil burn-down spreadsheet to account for temporary oncall delta.
sam: will keep oncall team posted during canary window.
maria: thanks all — will update sales and reopen if schedule slips.
